demands.decision: Decide whether the available representation actually separates the outcomes the problem asks for. Trace the observation, retained coordinates and expected label on unfamiliar rows.
demands.minimum: Provide different-class inputs whose observed coordinates coincide, explain why one deterministic rule cannot give both answers, find all such pairs on new data and reason about adding a coordinate.
demands.ceiling: Do not require a learned image encoder or a demonstration of generalization from a finite table in this week.
demands.counterexample: Identifying the largest entry of a supplied score row alone can succeed without representing either input. A chosen two-coordinate projection can collapse labels that the original images distinguish.
demands.later_use: Week 2 feature selection and evaluation require checking which information is available when predicting; later classification and retrieval need a feature representation matched to the objective.

demands.decision: Choose a row, column, observed denominator or ordered summary according to the data and the requested output.
demands.minimum: Explain one axis reduction by name and units, distinguish observed zero from missing, and compare class- or group-specific counts or percentages on a changed example.
demands.ceiling: No estimate of population performance is required from a few rows. The original audio task does not turn signal reconstruction into a Week 1 requirement.
demands.counterexample: Different sequences can have the same mean, and a group with fewer matching cases can have a higher within-group rate.
demands.later_use: Week 2 requires an appropriate scoring denominator and preprocessing; later time-series and attention topics use structure beyond simple means.

demands.decision: Connect a visible training-derived quantity to a prediction and to its held-out evaluation using explicitly available features.
demands.minimum: Calculate class centers from labeled training values and compare squared distances on a fresh sample. Distinguish an unknown class from a missing feature or true zero. Explain why changing a held-out answer can change the measured score while leaving the prediction fixed.
demands.ceiling: Retain these mathematical decisions using first-week operations. Course topic KOAI-04 practical estimator interfaces are taught beginning Week 2. Do not require a student to follow fit/predict, a learned imputer or pipeline as a prerequisite for the first-week answer. The competition's semi-supervised task is a later extension.
demands.counterexample: A correct call to a provided estimator may produce the target labels without identifying a training mean, a distance or the training-only boundary. Treating Antique unknown zero as the replica class changes the training problem.
demands.later_use: Week 2 introduces split-dependent transformations, and later weeks automate fitted models using scikit-learn. The first-week calculation supplies an interpretable check of that automation.

demands.decision: Identify which object each feature row and returned answer refer to, and use the comparison warranted by the problem.
demands.minimum: On a fresh input keep rows, feature names, predictions and original request order aligned. Explain when a dot product and length-normalized score can choose different candidates.
demands.ceiling: Do not require the original full contest training strategy or packaging procedure to demonstrate the representation principle.
demands.counterexample: Reordering only the label identifiers while retaining the old scores or features changes the meaning of an apparently valid numeric answer.
demands.later_use: Weeks 4 and 10 compare predictions with the correct examples and preserve the delivery order prescribed by an unfamiliar task.
